altbuild: none: pip-wrapped Python package, one pinned wheel image.

comparison.rule: Every sorted eigenvalue of H(t=0) is graded pointwise, |c-r|<=atol+rtol|r|; nothing excluded.

configuration: spin_basis_1d(L=4, kblock=0, pblock=1); H(t)=zz(J)+z(h)+x(g,cos(Omega t)-driven); sorted spectrum of H(t=0).
default_vs_upstream: Upstream only constructs H and prints the basis (no numeric output); this check diagonalises H(t=0) and grades the sorted spectrum. This is the same model and parameters as doc-hamiltonian (which additionally sets static_fmt='dia', a storage-format choice with no physical effect); the two checks share this path deliberately -- they are distinct documented decks (one demonstrates spin_basis_1d, the other the hamiltonian dia format) but compute the same physics.

evidence.floor_how: no alternative build; the nominal/variant self-validation measures the spread

observable: spectrum_t0: the full sorted eigenvalue spectrum of H evaluated at t=0.
variant: The transverse-drive amplitude g changes from g=0.809 to g*(1+1e-13) (relative 1e-13); g multiplies the off-diagonal x operator.
warrant: A wrong Hamiltonian construction, operator string, drive evaluation or eigensolver changes the t=0 spectrum far beyond the measured bound; a correct but differently-ordered summation stays inside it -- the active-g variant supplies the calibration evidence.
